source.title: On the Computational Inefficiency of Large Batch Sizes for Stochastic Gradient Descent
source.authors: Noah Golmant; N. Vemuri; Zhe-Wei Yao; Vladimir Feinberg; A. Gholami; Kai Rothauge; Michael W. Mahoney; Joseph E. Gonzalez

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether batch size affects held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets, using experiments across batch sizes and learning-rate strategies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports separate test accuracies for ResNet34 on CIFAR-10 in Table 2. Other cited findings are prior work, not this study’s results. Figure 5 reports test-loss contours, but does not provide extractable numeric values.
record.test_reason: The study directly varies SGD batch size under fixed epoch budgets and measures held-out accuracy, testing V5 with the same basic method and measure as its original image-classification studies. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but omits the central conclusion: increasing batch size eventually gives little or no convergence-time benefit and increases computational cost, even assuming perfect parallelism. The tested heuristics do not solve this convergence problem and usually improve generalization only at small-to-medium batch sizes.
record.recipe_differences: Compared batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets using BLR and linear scaling with warm-up, whereas the version summarizes several studies and adaptive recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies with batch size and learning-rate strategy. The paper also reports differing convergence behavior across model architectures and dataset complexity; Figure 3 contains those comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: Iteration-based convergence speed saturates beyond a workload-dependent batch size, even assuming perfect parallelism.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large-batch training has diminishing computational returns whose threshold depends on architecture and data complexity.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear approximation error increases as test accuracy deteriorates under linear learning-rate scaling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Failure of a local linear approximation accompanies the breakdown of linear learning-rate scaling.

fits_no_version.finding: DRN-D-22 on Cityscapes has batch-dependent training and test-loss convergence behavior.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large batches can impair optimization and held-out performance in image segmentation.

record.problems: Table 2 reports no uncertainty estimates. The directly extractable test-accuracy comparison is one model and dataset; the additional test-loss comparisons appear only as contour plots.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 5 has test-loss contours for ResNet34 on CIFAR-10, LSTM on WikiText-2, and DRN-D-22 on Cityscapes, under BLR and LSR. Values are figure-only and are not separately extracted because the text provides no model-specific numeric test-loss values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width increases beyond the width needed for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, broader optimizer tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers.

Normalization or regularization changes as remedies, and successful elimination of the penalty within the same epoch budget. Language-model test losses are studied in Figure 5 but not numerically recoverable from the supplied text.
Dropout's effect on held-out error and its dependence on dataset size or other regularization.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with train-test gaps, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: The authors report their own longer-training experiments and state that extra training often did not improve final test performance. Add this qualitative result with model, batch size, and extended budget marked unspecified; it cannot establish a model-specific verdict.
missing.locator: Section 4 opening paragraph; Section 2, Training longer

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 values are correctly transcribed. Divergence demonstrates worse held-out performance but does not isolate a generalization effect from optimization failure. Figure 5 is already declared in rows_left_out, so it is not listed as missing; its contour values cannot be recovered from the supplied text. E2's row links should refer to LSR rows R18–R20 rather than BLR rows R1–R10.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning or switching optimizers.
Language models; comparison with smaller batches beyond the reported ResNet34/CIFAR-10 test accuracies; whether normalization or regularization changes remove the penalty.
Dropout and its interaction with training set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures as correlates of the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
